package_info.why_malicious: Versions 1.1.5, 1.1.6, and 1.1.7 of @ledgerhq/connect-kit were published to npm using compromised credentials. These versions included a tampered WalletConnect integration that, at runtime, redirected user cryptocurrency transactions to an attacker-controlled wallet address, resulting in active theft of user funds.

execution_context.file_location: src/integrations/walletconnect.js (or equivalent WalletConnect integration file within the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts WalletConnect session events, programmatically replaces the legitimate destination wallet address with a hardcoded attacker-controlled address, and causes all user-initiated transactions to be redirected to the attacker's wallet.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code actively modifies the destination wallet address during live WalletConnect sessions, which is a direct violation of expected transaction integrity and is a hallmark of man-in-the-middle attacks targeting cryptocurrency theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate WalletConnect integrations should securely relay user-specified wallet addresses and transaction details without alteration. Modifying the destination address in production code, especially to a hardcoded value, is never acceptable and directly undermines user trust and security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, address redirection may occur in test environments or for QA purposes, but such logic should never be present in production releases or without explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Runtime interception and modification of wallet addresses in WalletConnect sessions
Presence of hardcoded, non-official wallet addresses within integration code
Tampering with transaction destination logic to redirect funds
Absence of user notification or consent for address changes

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains npm publishing credentials for @ledgerhq/connect-kit via spear phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish unauthorized package versions.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious versions 1.1.5, 1.1.6, and 1.1.7 of @ledgerhq/connect-kit containing altered WalletConnect integration code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package versions become available to the public.

attack_chain.action: Developers and end users install or update to the compromised package versions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is deployed and ready to execute on user systems.

attack_chain.action: During runtime, the malicious code intercepts WalletConnect sessions and replaces the intended wallet address with the attacker's address, redirecting user funds.
Ledger and WalletConnect respond by releasing a clean version and advising users to avoid affected versions and review recent transactions.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime modification of wallet addresses within WalletConnect session handlers
Assignment of hardcoded wallet addresses in transaction logic
Unexpected changes to transaction destination addresses after package update
Absence of user prompts or notifications when transaction destinations are altered
file_indicators: Altered or newly introduced code in src/integrations/walletconnect.js or similar integration files
Presence of hardcoded wallet address strings not matching official Ledger documentation
Unexpected diffs in WalletConnect-related files between versions 1.1.4 and 1.1.5+
network_indicators: Outbound transactions or API calls to wallet addresses not previously associated with Ledger or user accounts
Spike in transactions to a single, previously unseen wallet address immediately after package update
Unusual transaction patterns or destinations following installation of affected package versions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for code changes in WalletConnect integration files, especially for hardcoded wallet addresses that do not match official Ledger documentation. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized modifications in critical package files. Flag any runtime assignment or modification of wallet addresses in session handlers. Alert on outbound transactions to new or unrecognized wallet addresses following package updates. Correlate package update events with changes in transaction destinations to identify potential compromise.
